item.description: Help Net Security: Xalgorix, an open-source AI penetration testing tool, checks its work before it reports anything. When its main agent finds a bug, a second agent has to exploit that bug again. If the second agent can’t prove the bug is real or rule it out, Xalgorix keeps the finding and flags it for a person to review. item.title: Hackers Direct AI Agents to Break Into University Networks, Discovering Zero-Day Along the Way
item.description: GBHackers: A Chinese-nexus actor who used an autonomous AI penetration-testing framework to attack East Asian universities. The agents found and exploited a previously unknown vulnerability in an open-source medical imaging application. The operator’s only goal was “obtain shell access.” On September 10, 2026, Amazon found a publicly reachable Cairn instance running without authentication.
